Maria (runtime): heads up — noticed a weird sawtooth in kv cache resident set on Dedicated after the kernel bump yesterday. memory grows steadily during long contexts then drops ~15% every ~20m. only seen on Dedicated and our onprem lab, not on Hosted. :thinking:

Ajay (infra): more context? same model, same batch sizes? any config drift between dedicated and hosted?

Maria (runtime): same model and runtime binary. batching window unchanged. Dedicated uses our reserved pools (nvlink topology), Hosted is containerized on cloud gpus. differences i can think of: kernel 6.1 -> 6.4 on dedicated hosts, hugepage settings, cgroup v2 mem controller differences, and VPC MTU on hosted which might affect pagewalk timings (wtf but plausible).

Sam (ml): saw similar long-context growth in canaries last month but it leveled — this one keeps climbing until eviction kicks in and then it drops (but application latency spikes right when it drops). can you paste a perf report?

Maria (runtime): pasted small perf snippet and pmap after 40m run:

```
# perf report (top flame)
kv_cache_pagewalk  34.1%  libkv.so
kv_slot_reuse      12.8%  libkv.so
page_fault_handler 9.5%   kernel
copy_user          7.6%   kernel
```

pmap snippet:
```
00007f8a0000-00007f8bffff rw-p   1.2G  kvcache
resident: 1.1G   anon: 900M   file: 200M
```

Ajay (infra): can you also share slabinfo / vmstat around the drop? suspect fragmentation + madvise coalescing not happening on that kernel. different GLIBC madvise semantics could delay MADV_DONTNEED leading to apparent growth until eviction.

Maria (runtime): vmstat during growth:
```
procs ---memory-- ---swap-- -----io---- -system-- ------cpu-----
 r  b   swpd   free   buff  cache   si   so    bi    bo   in   cs us sy id wa
 2  0  0  250M  12M  1.1G  0    0     120   45   100  320  18  6  60 16
```
Then right after the drop: free jumps + cached drops, io spikes ~600kb/s.

Leo (sre): interesting that Hosted doesn't show it. Hosted uses cgroup-managed containers and we pin some kernel boot params at cloud provider level. Dedicated (baremetal) likely has NUMA/hugepage differences. Could be page fragmentation causing pagewalks to be expensive and the runtime triggers a conservative eviction that causes latency.

Sam (ml): does our kv cache use a shadow-paging strategy (we call it "shadowpages" internally) where we keep a logical view and only materialize pages on access? If materialization path differs (hugepage vs normal) we might be crossing a threshold where pages get mapped non-contiguously and trigger expensive TLB misses.

Maria (runtime): yes, we do shadowpages for long contexts — we lazily map slots for KV frames. I instrumented the map path: mapping rate stays constant but pmap churn increases. evict path triggered by background sweeper which looks at residency and last-access. timing of sweeper differs across hosts.

Ajay (infra): quick repro plan: run the same long-context replay on a Dedicated host with kernel 6.4 and on a Hosted container with 6.1 if possible. also try toggling vm.zone_reclaim_mode and vm.vfs_cache_pressure and see if behavior changes.

Maria (runtime): scheduled replay run (attached run id kv/4953). early observations: increasing slab_min_size seems to reduce the amplitude of the sawtooth but not eliminate growth. disabling hugepages entirely on dedicated removed the big drops but overall resident was slightly higher and latency improved.

Leo (sre): disabling hugepages might remove coalescing mismatch at expense of higher page table overhead — explains higher resident but less eviction panic. We should avoid recommending that as prod fix. maybe a runtime mitigation: more aggressive background unlock-and-scan when we detect long tail reuse patterns?

Sam (ml): could batching heuristics be contributing? if autobatcher delays token emission and we accumulate bigger KV blocks before map, the map pattern changes. any correlation between big batching windows and the drop times?

Maria (runtime): yes — the waveform aligns with autoscaling bursts and big batch flushes. When we get large flush events, we materialize many shadow pages quickly and then sweeper runs to trim them. On Dedicated the sweeper stalls (likely due to pagewalk latency) and triggers a cliff eviction. Hosted sweeper is faster because cgroup page reclaim is more responsive there.

Ajay (infra): two action items: 1) kernel bisect candidate: revert the recent memory reclaim patch on our Dedicated kernel in canary. 2) runtime change: add a staggered materialize flag so we spread mapping of shadowpages over X ms instead of all at once. could dramatically reduce sweep pressure.

Maria (runtime): working on a PR for staggered materialize (small diffuser). will run A/B with and without on dedicated canary.

ciara-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout for runtime:v3.8-stagger started on dedicated-pool-3 (rollout id r-8347).

Leo (sre): also let's collect per-page pte walk latencies using perf PMU on dedicated niceties — i'll attach a job to collect pagemap/ptwalk samples during next run.

Sam (ml): if the stagger trick works, we should still keep an opt-in hugepage-aware allocator that prefers contiguous mappings when nvlink/NUMA suggests lower pagewalk cost. but default to stagger for safety.

Maria (runtime): agreed. I'll post perf diffs once canary finishes (run ~30m). thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Ajay (infra): great notes — adding followups to infra runbook: kernel-reclaim-bisect, hugepage policy checklist, and a VPC/MTU oddness note.

Leo (sre): filing a short postmortem draft if canary shows regressions. but so far looks like config+kernel interaction + batching pattern = eviction jitter.

Maria (runtime): final note — folks hitting similar symptoms: try toggling vm.vfs_cache_pressure down to 50 and enable staged materialize locally. I'll share the PR link when available.
